notes: flow-check: any site may be a check target (no live-site rule, no allowlist) and the preview adopts the whole .env of the connected project with no exemption (afb-checks 1.9.0, AFB-20261022-2332).

flow-check: an app that signs in only by an emailed link gets its mail settings sealed (POSTMARK_*, with a test inbox and the owner's test-token word); the preview mails only that inbox, and a person runs login (AFB-20261022-0518).

flow, flow-check: the UI shots feature is gone (no ui_shots_run, ui_shots_get or ui_changes_save, no UI shots tab); a check's screenshots show as pictures on the item's Checks tab, so flow loses step 5b and flow-check gains a Screenshots section (AFB-20261022-2318).

Prompt diet (AFB-20261022-0217). Skip workflow_get when the skill is installed. Shared rules block removed from flow and flow-audit and shortened for the others. flow-critic size gate (1 subagent for a small diff, pass 2 only after a blocker, no question about the mode). flow: small work is plan and approval at once, critic only for 4+ steps, audit once per item, one defaults-versus-questions rule, a typed deploy request is the confirmation, no browser steps unless asked. Safety text kept once in flow and pointed to from the other skills.

UI shots capture themselves. flow: after a finished screen change call ui_shots_run with wait (step 5b), no pages and no table; flow-check: the UI shots section says the tool finds the changed screens, builds the last commit as the Before and reports plain notes. ui_changes_save only pins an extra page.

flow-check: several afb-checks registrations (repo folders) for one board project. Register the second folder with --board-project, name the registration on check_save or check_run, read runner_status registrations; a run with several registrations and none named is refused with REGISTRATION_REQUIRED and the list; project forget lets go of a registration. flow: one line in step 5a pointing at it.

flow: new Keep going rule. Once the user approves or says proceed, every phase runs to the end without stopping or asking to continue, and the only stops are a decision that is the user's, a safety rule, a tool error or a real block. A request to plan and build skips the approval wait. Questions the user's words, the code or earlier decisions can answer are decided and recorded, not asked. The same rules are in the shared workflow rules every harness gets.
flow-check: the afb-checks tool of 1.3.1 no longer carries the move from an older layout (migrate command, old credential file, checks/<item> folder); an install still on 1.2.x must be set up again.

flow-check: one afb-checks tool serves every organisation. Connecting another organisation adds a connection and never replaces one, a project is org/KEY, checks live in checks/<org>/<item>/, the worker takes several runs at once and every run has its own copy, port, browser and database. runner_status shows capacity. New run codes SANDBOX_FAILED and DOCKER_DOWN.

flow: the skills notice points at the flow_skills tool of the connection, whose reply carries the steps; the separate flow-skills skill is gone because a skill must be installed before anyone can find it, so the installer is now an MCP tool.

flow: a skillsNotice from session_start is told to the user once, with an offer to install or update the skills through the new flow_skills and skills_file tools of the MCP, on one yes without more questions (new item 7 of section 0).

flow: a step with a requiredTarget, or an automatic check, is handed to /flow-check with the item, the check key and the step (new step 5a); it is never ticked by hand without run evidence; a repo rulebook that forbids browser checks, or a user who did not ask for one, leaves it as a manual check.
flow-check: new "Called from /flow" section. flow-audit: an automatic check or requiredTarget step with no passing run is reopened.

All skills: now generic. They name no repo, path, branch, port, project key or gate command of their own. The project key is found from what the user names, the repo rulebook or board_brief; the gates come from the repo rulebook or package scripts, and when none are found the skill says so and asks.

All skills: the repo rulebook (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README, project rules) overrides project facts and optional steps, never the safety rules: no commit or push without the user's word, no branch changes, nothing live or non-local without confirmation, no database reset, no tokens or .env values, no AI attribution.
flow-critic: every lens and lane is kept; stack-specific items now say when they apply and carry a labelled example. The subagent prompt takes a {PROJECT_DESCRIPTION} placeholder.
If your repo relied on the old built-in overrides (no UI changes table, no browser checks in plans, branch main), put them in your CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.

flow: no usage tools any more. usage_report and the usage field of item_get are gone from the board; remove coding tool exporter env vars and the OpenCode plugin file that sent usage to the board (they now get a 404).
flow-audit, flow-check, flow-critic, flow-interview, flow-task, flow-verify: wording updates made in the same working tree, not part of the usage removal.
flow: usage_report stores a cost only when the agent passes costUsd; the board keeps no price table.
flow: names the MCP tool usage_report and item_get fields [usage], for agents whose tool exports no usage.

flow-check: rewritten for the hands-off afb-checks tool (an agent connects, repairs and upgrades it; it stops only for 5433, 5180, 5190 or a live site). Bundle 1.0.0 was never published, so its flow-check text was amended in place and keeps version 1.0.0.
First release of the system skills bundle.
